title: New knowledge domains (2026-09-14 expansion) — OWASP LLM Top 10, capa, Threat Hunter Playbook, Windows/AD security
description: Locally-authored, deterministic retrieval cases for the four sources added in the 2026-09-14 knowledge expansion (owasp-llm-top10-src, capa-rules-src, threathunter-playbook-src, windows-ad-security-docs-src). Kept as a SEPARATE suite from retrieval-100k-v1 so the historical 118-case suite stays byte-for-byte unchanged and its before/after comparison remains valid. Every case here was verified against live retrieval before being added — none were kept by adjusting wording until they happened to pass; several candidate cases (an AMSI-patch case with a hyphenation-sensitive substring, two more Threat Hunter Playbook queries, a UPX case with generic wording) were tried, found to genuinely miss, and were either fixed for a real assertion-matching bug (not a retrieval change) or dropped rather than forced. threathunter-playbook-src is real and correctly licensed but is by far the smallest of the four new packs (530 chunks) and loses ranking competition against much larger pre-existing detection packs (e.g. splunk-security-content-src, 14,574 chunks) for anything but its most distinctive hunts — only one of four candidate queries for that pack reliably won its top-5; this is reported as an honest capacity/competitiveness finding, not fixed here. KNOWN GAP: no case in this suite tests genuine insufficient-evidence behavior at the retrieval layer, because `services/knowledge/retrieval.py`'s `retrieve()` has no relevance-score cutoff — it returns its best-effort top-k for literally any query as long as at least one pack is enabled, and returns `[]` only when no packs are enabled at all (verified: a fictional-CVE query and an unrelated-domain query both still returned five non-empty, topically-unrelated results). Honest insufficient-evidence behavior is therefore a property of the answer-synthesis layer, not retrieval, and cannot be tested by this retrieval-only harness — see `score_case()`'s new optional `expect_insufficient` field in harness.py, added for this purpose but left unused here since no genuine retrieval-level case for it exists; a real test would need to exercise the actual chat/ask() completion path with an LLM call.

cases.query: What is LLM01 prompt injection in the OWASP Top 10 for LLM applications?
OWASP LLM Top 10 sensitive information disclosure risk in LLM applications
What is excessive agency risk for LLM-powered autonomous agents per OWASP?
capa rule for patching the AMSI Antimalware Scan Interface function to bypass detection
malware technique that checks for sandbox and antivirus modules before running
YARA rule detecting UPX packed or obfuscated binaries
cases.note: Same query as the yara-packer case in retrieval-100k-v1 — deliberately reused here as a positive case against capa-rules-src specifically, since the regression investigation established capa's packed-with-upx.yml (a stable, non-quarantined rule) is genuinely the more precise answer; see AI_HANDOFF.md Priority 1 writeup.

cases.query: threat hunting technique for DLL process injection via CreateRemoteThread and LoadLibrary
What is Active Directory Certificate Services and how does it work?
explain certificate templates concepts in Active Directory Certificate Services
How do I configure Kerberos delegation for group Managed Service Accounts in Active Directory?
ESC1 Active Directory Certificate Services misconfiguration privilege escalation attack
cases.note: Deliberately difficult/ambiguous case: Microsoft's own AD CS documentation (windows-ad-security-docs-src) explains how the feature works but does not use offensive-security terminology like 'ESC1' (that vocabulary comes from external attack research, e.g. Certified Pre-Owned). The CORRECT sources for an attack-technique query like this are detection/attack-mapping packs, not the vendor feature docs — this case verifies the system distinguishes 'how a feature works' documentation from 'how to detect abuse of that feature' content rather than matching indiscriminately on shared keywords like 'Active Directory Certificate Services'.
